content: keyd/xremap coexistence: keyd remaps at kernel evdev/uinput layer (system-wide daemon, layers/oneshot/macros); IBus operates at display-server/application level; no structural conflict because they occupy different layers - remapped events flow through libinput/mutter before IBus sees them. Caveat: keyd can grab uinput devices of OTHER injectors (feedback loop, needs exclusion config, per Mouseless docs), which matters for the ydotool e2e path when keyd is enabled; an IME must configure hotkeys in terms of POST-remap keys. goswitch as IBus engine never opens evdev, so it cannot conflict with keyd/xremap.
